title: Part One, Chapter 2: The Animals, the Man of Mud and the Men of Wood

verses.t: And then they conceived the animals of the forest, the guardians of all the mountains, the creatures of the wilds: the deer, the bird, the puma, the jaguar, the serpent, the viper, the cantí snake, the guardians of the vines. And the Creator said, "Shall there be only silence and stillness beneath the trees and vines? It is better that there be something to guard them." They say that they discussed it and spoke together, and then the deer and the birds were brought forth, and then they gave the deer and the birds their dwellings: "You, deer, shall sleep along the paths of the water and in the ravines; here you shall live among the grass and the weeds; in the forest you shall multiply; on four feet you shall walk, and on four feet you shall stand." So it was said to them, and their homes were fixed for the great and small birds as well: "You birds shall make your houses and dwellings upon the trees and vines, and there you shall multiply and shake yourselves upon the branches of the trees and vines." This was said to the deer and the birds, who then did as they were told. All of them took their sleeping places and their dwellings, and so the earth was given them for a home by the Creator, once all the deer and the birds had been finished.

Then the Creator and Former spoke once more to the deer and the birds: "Speak, call out; do not just make 'yol, yol'; do not merely cry out, but speak, each according to its kind and its difference." It was said to the deer and the birds, to the pumas, jaguars and serpents: "Say our name, praise us, say that we are your mothers and your fathers, Huracán, Chipa-caculha, Raxa-caculha, Heart of the Sky, Heart of the Earth, the Formers, the Creators, the mothers and fathers; speak, call on us, greet us," it was said to them. But they could not speak like men; they only screeched, cackled and cried out, saying "voh, voh." No speech appeared; each one screeched and cried in its own way. And when the Formers heard that they did not speak, they said again among themselves, "It has not been possible for them to say our name, though we are their Formers and Creators. This is not good," those Formers said among themselves. And it was said to the animals: "You shall be changed, because you could not speak; so we have changed our word. Your food, your pasture, your sleeping places and dwellings shall be the ravines and the forests, because you have not managed to greet us; you have not called on us. There shall yet be someone who calls on us; we shall make others who will obey us. Accept this lot: your flesh shall be chewed, and for that you shall serve." So it was said to them, and so it was announced to all the animals, small and great, that are upon the earth. And then they wished to try their fortune again; they wished to try once more, and to join again in greeting, but they could not understand one another's speech, and in no way was it right or possible. And so their flesh was scorned and cast aside; they paid tribute; all the animals here upon the earth were eaten and killed. And so the Creator tried once more to make other creatures: "Let us try again; the sowing and the dawn are drawing near. Let us make one who will sustain and nourish us. How shall we be called upon and remembered upon the earth? We have already tried our first works and formed beings, and we could not bring them to praise us and to honour us. So let us try to make obedient ones who will sustain us." They say that it was formed and made of earth. All of it was made, its body; but it did not look well. It kept coming apart; it was soft and lumpy and limp; it crumbled and grew wet. Its head did not move; its face stayed turned to one side; it was blind and could not look behind it. Though it spoke, it had no understanding; it dissolved in the water; it was not strong. And the Makers and Formers said again, "It will only get worse; it will not walk or multiply. Let it be made only of its own understanding," so they said. And then they undid it and kneaded it again, their formed and fashioned thing, and said, "How shall we make it again, so that it can praise us and call on us?" They say that they held council again: "We shall tell Xpiyacoc and Xmucane, and Hun-ahpu-vuch and Hun-ahpu-uhú; let us try our fortune again." The Formers and Fashioners spoke of its making to one another, and then they told it to Xpiyacoc and Xmucane, and afterwards it was told to the diviners, the grandmother of the day or sun and of the moon, as they were called by the Makers and Fashioners; these were the names of Xpiyacoc and Xmucane. And that Huracán, with Tepeu and Cucumatz, spoke to the diviner of the sun, to the diviner who forms; the matter reached her and was joined to it again: "Let our formed man be made again, our built man, one again who will sustain and nourish us, who will call on us and remember us. Enter into the council, our grandmother and grandfather, Xpiyacoc and Xmucane: how can it be sown and made to dawn, so that we are called upon, adored and remembered by man, formed and built, by our poor man? And so let it be said; show your names, Hun-ahpu-vuch, Hun-ahpu-uhú, twice mother, twice father, great coati, you of the jade stones, you of the jeweller's drill, you of the board, the other one, you of the toltecat, grandmother of the sun, grandmother of the moon; so may you be called by those we form and create. Cast lots with maize and with tzité beans, and let it be done: shall it come out, shall we carve and shape its mouth and face from wood?" So it was said to the diviners. And then came the casting of the lots, the greeting of what they drew with the maize and the tzité, to the sun, to the formed one. An old woman and an old man spoke to them; the old man was the one of the tzité lots and was called Xpiyacoc, and the old woman, the diviner of the sun and of the formed one, was called Chiracan-xmucane. And they say that they began to divine the sun: "Come together, be joined; tell us your news, our hearing; speak, talk, whether it is fitting that the wood be carved by the Formers, and whether this is the one who is to sustain and nourish, that it may be sown and dawn. Speak, you maize; you, tzité; you, sun; you, formed one; call out and go on," she said to the maize and the tzité, to the sun and the formed one. "And you, Heart of the Sky, be ashamed; do not put Tepeu and Cucumatz to shame." And then the tzité and the maize answered and spoke the truth: "Do it so, and so it will be well; the wood will speak when it is carved." And then the image of the man of wood was made, and it spoke like a man. And this was the man they made, and they multiplied and had sons and daughters; but they turned out foolish, without heart, without understanding, and so they did not remember their Creator any more, but lived and walked upon the earth in vain, and did not remember the Heart of the Sky any more, and so they fell upon their faces. This was only a trial, an attempt to make people stand and to make mankind. They spoke, but their faces were dry; they were clumsy and heavy in feet and hands; they had no blood, nor sweat, nor fat; their cheeks were dry and pale, their feet yellow, their hands dry, and their flesh yellow; and so they no longer remembered their Creator and Maker, the one who had created them. And they were already many, and they multiplied upon the earth.
